item.title: Indonesia Begins Purchases of Community-Managed Crude Oil
item.description: Jambi. Indonesia on Wednesday marked a milestone in formalizing community-run oil production as state energy company Pertamina completed its first-ever purchase of crude produced from community-managed oil wells, or sumur rakyat, in Jambi. item.title: Indonesia Eximbank Demonstrates Good Practice in Risk Governance
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia Eximbank (Lembaga Pembiayaan Ekspor Indonesia or LPEI) announced Wednesday that it had achieved the good practice phase category in the 2025 Risk Maturity Assessment (RMA) conducted by independent consultant RWI Consulting. The assessment shows that the agency has effectively implemented and integrated risk governance aspects, including processes, work culture, and organizational performance. item.title: Over 150 Prosecutors, Staff Disciplined by Indonesia’s Attorney General
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s Attorney General’s Office has imposed disciplinary sanctions on 101 prosecutors and 56 non-prosecutorial staff throughout 2025, as authorities step up internal oversight, an official said on Wednesday. item.title: Prabowo Visits Disaster-Hit Sumatra, Skips Palace New Year Celebration
item.description: South Tapanuli, North Sumatra. President Prabowo Subianto spent New Year’s Eve in South Tapanuli Regency, one of the areas hardest hit by floods and landslides in Sumatra, choosing to welcome the year alongside affected residents, officials said on Wednesday. During the visit, Prabowo inspected the construction of an emergency bridge over the Garoga River, built to restore connectivity after the original bridge was destroyed by flash floods. item.title: Prosecutors Recover Rp 19.6 Trillion in State Assets From Corruption Cases
item.description: Jakarta. The Attorney General’s Office recovered Rp 19.6 trillion ($1.2 billion) in state assets in 2025 from corruption and other financial crime cases that have received final and binding court rulings, an official said on Wednesday. item.title: New Year Celebrations Scaled Back Across Indonesia in Solidarity With Sumatra
item.description: Jakarta. Cities across Indonesia welcomed the start of 2026 with subdued New Year’s Eve observances, scaling back festivities and cancelling fireworks as a gesture of solidarity with victims of floods and landslides in Sumatra, where disasters have killed more than 1,100 people. item.title: Thailand Releases 18 Cambodian Prisoners of War as Part of Ceasefire Agreement
item.description: Phnom Penh. Thailand on Wednesday released 18 Cambodian prisoners of war held for five months, fulfilling the terms of a ceasefire agreement the two countries signed to end bitter fighting along their border. item.title: Parliamentary, Judicial Complexes in Nusantara to Be Ready Before 2028 Relocation
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia is targeting the completion of key central government buildings in its new capital, Nusantara, by the end of 2027, ahead of the planned relocation from Jakarta, Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka said on Wednesday. item.title: Photos: Drones Paint Jakarta’s Skyline in Place of Fireworks on New Year’s Eve
item.description: Jakarta. As the clock struck midnight to welcome 2026, Jakarta skipped its usual fireworks display and opted for a drone show instead, in a gesture of solidarity with disaster victims in Sumatra. Hundreds of illuminated drones took to the night sky in synchronized formations, creating striking visuals and messages such as “Jakarta for Sumatra” and “Road to Jakarta 500” above Bundaran Hotel Indonesia.
